text: No erp entry with purchase_order equal to the invoice purchase_order may have status 'PAGADA' (the order must not already be paid).
norm_rule_text: Estado ERP del pedido: PENDIENTE. Nunca pagar dos veces el mismo pedido.

norm_rules.text: Pagar solo si el NIF esta en el maestro y el IBAN de la factura coincide con el maestro.

checks.text: The invoice issuer_nif (normalised: uppercase, without spaces, hyphens or dots) must match the nif of a row in suppliers.
checks.interpretation: 'el NIF esta en el maestro' means the invoice issuer_nif must be found among the suppliers.nif values (the master of suppliers). The sentence only states the condition ('pagar solo si'), it does not name the outcome of failing it, so the decision is the policy default NO_PAGAR.

checks.text: The invoice iban (normalised: uppercase, without spaces) must equal the iban of the supplier in suppliers whose nif matches the invoice issuer_nif.
checks.interpretation: 'el IBAN de la factura coincide con el maestro' means the invoice iban must equal the suppliers.iban of the supplier identified by the invoice issuer_nif. Condition only, no outcome named, so policy default NO_PAGAR.

norm_rules.text: El pedido debe existir, pertenecer al proveedor y el importe de la factura debe ser igual al del pedido (tolerancia 0,01 EUR).

checks.text: The invoice purchase_order (normalised: uppercase, without spaces) must exist as a purchase_order in orders.
checks.interpretation: 'El pedido debe existir' means the invoice purchase_order must be present in orders.purchase_order. Condition only, no outcome named, so policy default NO_PAGAR.

checks.text: The order in orders with purchase_order equal to the invoice purchase_order must belong to the supplier: its supplier_id must equal the id of the supplier in suppliers whose nif matches the invoice issuer_nif.
checks.interpretation: 'pertenecer al proveedor' means the order's supplier_id must be the id of the supplier identified by the invoice issuer_nif. Condition only, no outcome named, so policy default NO_PAGAR.

checks.text: The invoice total must match the total_amount of the order in orders with the same purchase_order within ±0.01 EUR (abs(cents(total) - cents(total_amount)) <= 1).
checks.interpretation: 'el importe de la factura debe ser igual al del pedido (tolerancia 0,01 EUR)' compares the invoice total with orders.total_amount using the ±0.01 EUR tolerance. Condition only, no outcome named, so policy default NO_PAGAR.

norm_rules.text: El IVA debe estar bien calculado y el total debe ser base + IVA, con la misma tolerancia de 0,01 EUR.

checks.text: The invoice vat_amount must equal base * vat_rate / 100 within ±0.01 EUR (abs(cents(vat_amount) - cents(base * vat_rate / 100)) <= 1).
checks.interpretation: 'El IVA debe estar bien calculado' means the printed vat_amount must equal base times vat_rate (a percentage, 21 = 21%) divided by 100, within the stated ±0.01 EUR tolerance. Condition only, no outcome named, so policy default NO_PAGAR.

checks.text: The invoice total must equal base + vat_amount within ±0.01 EUR (abs(cents(total) - cents(base + vat_amount)) <= 1).
checks.interpretation: 'el total debe ser base + IVA' means the printed total must equal base plus vat_amount within the same ±0.01 EUR tolerance. Condition only, no outcome named, so policy default NO_PAGAR.

norm_rules.text: La fecha debe ser valida y no futura.

checks.text: The invoice date must be a valid calendar date (a real YYYY-MM-DD date, not an impossible one such as 2026-02-31).
checks.interpretation: 'La fecha debe ser valida' means the invoice date must be a real calendar date. Condition only, no outcome named, so policy default NO_PAGAR.

checks.text: The invoice date must not be later than parameters.cut_off_date (date <= cut_off_date, compared as dates).
checks.interpretation: 'no futura' is read against the only reference date available, parameters.cut_off_date: the invoice date must not be after it. Condition only, no outcome named, so policy default NO_PAGAR.

norm_rules.text: Estado ERP del pedido: PENDIENTE. Nunca pagar dos veces el mismo pedido.

checks.text: The erp entry with purchase_order equal to the invoice purchase_order must have status 'PENDIENTE'.
checks.interpretation: 'Estado ERP del pedido: PENDIENTE' means the erp entry matching the invoice purchase_order must have status PENDIENTE. Condition only, no outcome named, so policy default NO_PAGAR.

checks.text: No erp entry with purchase_order equal to the invoice purchase_order may have status 'PAGADA' (the order must not already be paid).
checks.interpretation: 'Nunca pagar dos veces el mismo pedido' is a prohibition: it fires when an erp entry for the same purchase_order already has status PAGADA. The sentence states what must not happen, not the outcome of failing it, so policy default NO_PAGAR.

norm_rules.text: Cualquier anomalia que un humano deba ver: ESCALAR con motivo. Ante duda razonable, escalar antes que pagar.
policies: Any anomaly that a human must see must be escalated with a reason.
When in reasonable doubt, escalate rather than pay.

data.instructions:
You write the tests for ONE business rule, from its text and the process context only. You never see the code: your tests are the reference it must meet.

Write the tests (at least as many as asked below): each with `name` (unique), `instance_json` (JSON object), `sources_json` (JSON object), `others_json` (JSON list) and `fires` (what the rule must return). Cover cases where it fires and where it does not, and the limits and exceptions the rule's text mentions. Use only the given symbol names as instance keys and only the given source names. Do not test a missing value unless the text or the description says what happens then.

The rule is evaluated by a Python function
`evaluate(instance, sources, others) -> {"fires": bool, "reason": str}`:
- `instance`: {symbol: value} of the instance being evaluated.
- `sources`: {source_name: [row, ...]}, each row a dict {column: value}.
- `others`: the other instances of the process, each {symbol: value} plus "_instance" (its name). Relevant only if the rule talks about other instances (duplicates, totals...).
- Rule type: `requirement` = something that must hold; it fires when it does NOT hold. `prohibition` = something that must not happen; it fires when it DOES happen.
- A value the rule needs may be missing or None. If the rule text or the use case description says what to do then, that is what happens. Otherwise the function raises, and the engine sends the instance to a person: it never guesses.

Use case description: conventions that apply to every rule of the use case (normalisation, units, tolerances...). Apply them before your own assumptions. If they contradict the rule's text, the rule's text wins.

If the rule needs data that is neither a symbol nor a source column, answer with NeedsData (what is missing and why) instead of inventing a field.

Write at least 6 tests.

## Guidance for this use case
Build test rows with the real column names of the sources shown. Include the limits the conventions define (exactly 1 cent of difference, normalised keys that only differ in spaces or case).
